Archicad: BIM Architectural Design and Documentation Suite for Windows 

 A Windows reference and setup guide for Graphisoft Archicad building information modeling software, design features, system profile, and the first-project workflow. 

 
 
 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Introduction

Archicad is Graphisoft's building information modeling (BIM) software for architects, designers, and construction professionals. It gives beginners a structured way to move from concept sketches to coordinated documentation, and it gives experienced professionals a deep toolset for complex, multi-disciplinary projects. Whether you are drafting your first floor plan or managing a large design team, the same unified model environment supports your work.

When you use Archicad, you build a single intelligent 3D model instead of disconnected drawings. Plans, sections, elevations, schedules, and renderings are all generated from that model, so changes propagate automatically across your documentation set. The typical workflow runs from schematic design through detailed modeling, then into documentation and finally into coordination and delivery.

In the architectural field, Archicad is known for its strong native BIM approach and its support for open standards such as IFC. The application is extensible through add-ons and third-party integrations, backed by a broad user community and professional training resources. It continues to evolve through regular releases that refine modeling, collaboration, and documentation tools.

 System Requirements

 Requirement Details 
 ------------- --------- 
 Supported Windows Versions Windows 10, Windows 11 
 Architecture x64 
 Processor Modern multi-core 64-bit processor (Intel Core i5/i7 or AMD Ryzen equivalent recommended) 
 RAM 8 GB minimum, 16 GB or more recommended for large BIM models 
 Storage Several GB free for the installation plus additional space for projects, libraries, and caches 
 Permissions Administrative privileges may be required 
 Internet Connection Required for activation and updates 
 Dependencies .NET Framework, Visual C++ Redistributable, up-to-date graphics driver with OpenGL support 

For the best performance in Archicad, focus your budget first on RAM and a solid-state drive, then on a capable dedicated GPU and a fast multi-core CPU. Large models with dense geometry, detailed libraries, and many linked files benefit most from additional memory and fast storage. On a machine near the minimum specs you can still work, but navigation, regeneration of views, and rendering will feel slower, especially as project complexity grows.

 Features

- BIM Model Authoring : Build a single intelligent 3D building model where walls, slabs, roofs, and openings behave as real architectural elements. This model becomes the source of truth for every drawing and schedule you produce.
- Parametric Object Library : Use built-in and custom parametric objects for doors, windows, furniture, and structure. Objects carry data and adapt to context, which keeps your model consistent and reduces repetitive editing.
- 2D and 3D Documentation : Generate plans, sections, elevations, and details directly from the model, then refine them with drafting tools. This keeps documentation aligned with the design at all times.
- Schedules and Quantities : Extract schedules for areas, components, and materials from the model. Architects and cost planners use these lists for specifications and quantity takeoffs without manual counting.
- Rendering and Visualization : Produce shaded views, internal renderings, and presentation-ready images from your model. This helps you communicate design intent to clients and collaborators early.
- Teamwork and Collaboration : Share a project through Teamwork so multiple team members can work on the same model with controlled access. This supports studios and larger offices that need coordinated concurrent editing.
- IFC and OpenBIM Exchange : Import and export IFC for coordination with engineers, consultants, and other BIM tools. Open exchange formats help you integrate Archicad into multi-software project pipelines.
- Add-ons and Extensibility : Extend the application with add-ons for specific workflows such as structural analysis support, energy evaluation, or data management. This lets you tailor the environment to the needs of a given project or office standard.

Community resources around Archicad are extensive, with active forums, video tutorial series, help centers, and user groups that cover both beginner questions and advanced workflows. This makes it easier to learn the basics and to keep growing your skills as projects become more demanding.

 How It Works

1. Installation : Download the installation package from the official source for Archicad. Run the installer and follow the on-screen instructions to complete setup. Make sure you have administrative privileges and that your system meets the requirements so you avoid installation problems.

2. Project Setup and Template Selection : Create a new project and choose a template that matches your region and office standards. Templates define units, pen sets, layer combinations, and libraries so your project starts with consistent conventions.

3. Modeling the Building : Lay out grid lines, levels, and stories, then add walls, slabs, roofs, and openings using the modeling tools. Parametric objects fill in doors, windows, and furnishings as your design develops.

4. Documentation and Detailing : Open the integrated documentation views to annotate plans, sections, and elevations generated from the model. Use schedules and detail tools to complete the drawing set and coordinate information.

5. Coordination and Delivery : Publish the model and drawings for consultants and clients, and exchange IFC files where coordination is required. Finalize plot sets, exports, and archived project files for handover.
